item.description:

West Norfolk students tackle hospital tech challenges
Students from five schools across West Norfolk are taking part in the Future Talent Tech Programme. The initiative, delivered by Tech Educators and funded by the local council, tasks young people with solving real-world problems faced by the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn.
Participants are attending workshops to develop skills in coding, AI, and project management. These sessions will continue throughout the autumn, helping students refine their ideas ahead of a final hackathon. item.title: Witnesses sought following hit-and-run in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Witnesses sought following hit-and-run in King’s Lynn
Norfolk Police are appealing for information after a hit-and-run incident in King’s Lynn on Sunday evening. At approximately 10:50pm, a dark-coloured 4x4 collided with a parked silver Suzuki Swift on Southgate Street, causing significant damage to the vehicle. Doorbell footage captured the collision, and officers are now working to identify the driver involved.
Anyone who witnessed the incident or possesses relevant dashcam footage is urged to contact Norfolk Police. You can assist the investigation by calling 01603 276220 or emailing RoadCollisionsSupportTeam@Suffolk.police.uk, quoting reference URN 1825752. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

item.title: New youth hub to open in Wisbech
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New youth hub to open in Wisbech
A new youth hub is opening in Wisbech to support young people aged 16 to 25 across Fenland. Based at the Annabelle Davis Centre on Love Lane, the facility aims to help those not currently in education, employment, or training. Run by the charity Centre 33 and backed by the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority, the hub will provide a single location for guidance on careers, skills, housing, and wellbeing. The project intends to reduce the number of young people struggling to access work by offering joined-up support. Outreach services will also be available to ensure those in rural communities can access help. Organisations interested in partnering with the hub are invited to make contact.

item.title: RSPCA appeals for support as seal entanglement cases rise
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
RSPCA appeals for support as seal entanglement cases rise
The RSPCA East Winch Wildlife Centre is calling for public support following the rescue of three seals in just three weeks. Each animal was found suffering from severe injuries caused by man-made debris, including fishing gear, a plastic bag, and a flying ring.
Centre manager Evangelos Achilleos says the animals face a critical recovery period due to exhaustion and deep wounds. The charity is now urging the public to sign a national petition calling for a ban on flying rings in the UK. Since 2008, the centre has treated over 100 seals for similar entanglement injuries. Donations to assist with the ongoing rehabilitation costs can be made via the RSPCA East Winch website.

item.title: King’s Lynn man jailed for stalking and racist abuse
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man jailed for stalking and racist abuse
A prolific offender from King’s Lynn has been sentenced to 32 weeks in prison following a trial at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. 52-year-old Dean Locke was found guilty of stalking his former partner and faced sentencing for 20 additional offences, including multiple assaults on police officers and incidents of racist abuse.
The court heard that Locke’s offences took place between May and September. Alongside the jail term, he has been issued with a two-year restraining order preventing contact with his ex-partner, and a 12-month order regarding a shop worker he targeted. Locke was also ordered to pay £100 in compensation to several of his victims.
